title: 3/recipient/hour fan-out bound is bypassable with concurrent claims — count subquery sees pre-burst snapshot
evidence:
UPDATE application_draft
SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, $3),
    last_link_sent_at = now()
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND email = lower($2)
  AND submitted_at IS NULL
  AND erased_at IS NULL
  AND (
    last_link_sent_at IS NULL
    OR last_link_sent_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'
  )
  AND (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  ) < 3
RETURNING COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token;
detail: Each claim UPDATE locks only its own (vacancy,email) row, so concurrent claims for the same recipient on different vacancies all evaluate the count subquery against the pre-burst committed state and all pass. A free landlord signup yields up to 20 unpaid vacancies; attacker saves one victim-email draft per vacancy (unauthenticated), then fires 20 concurrent POST /apply/:code/continue-link — victim gets up to 20 branded Resend emails in one burst despite the documented 3/hour bound.
recommended_fix: Serialize per recipient: take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(lower($2))) at the top of the claim statement, or record sends in a recipient_send_log table with an insert-then-count so concurrent claims conflict.

title: 500/vacancy draft cap is exhaustible by an unauthenticated attacker and fails silently with ok:true
evidence:
INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)
SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND d.email = lower($2)
  )
  OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
... handler: `Ok(_) -> { ... wisp.json_response(json_ok(True), 200) }`
detail: 500 unauthenticated POSTs with throwaway emails fill a vacancy's cap (no per-IP bound; Cloudflare edge rule deferred per spec). Legitimate first-time savers then get zero-row inserts the handler reports as ok:true — the client marks the payload acknowledged and announces rt:draft-saved, and the later continue-link answers sent:false while the UI says 'Link sent — check your inbox'. The count also includes submitted/erased tombstones, so filled slots are never reclaimed until vacancy close.
recommended_fix: Return a distinct ok:false/closed-style flag when the upsert inserted/updated zero rows so the client stops claiming success; count only live rows (submitted_at IS NULL AND erased_at IS NULL) toward the cap; track per-IP throttling for draft writes.

title: Non-empty junk payload still clobbers a victim's existing draft — empty-guard only blocks the '{}' wipe
detail: The guard acknowledges the unauthenticated destructive-write vector but only blocks the empty-map case: PUT /apply/:code/draft with {"email":"victim@x","fields":{"a":"b"}} wholesale-replaces the victim's saved answers (SET fields = EXCLUDED.fields, no token required). The victim's resume link then renders attacker-chosen values into their form (escaped, so no XSS, but e.g. an attacker phone number reaches the landlord if submitted unnoticed).
recommended_fix: On conflict for a row that already has a continue_token, require payload.resume_token to match before replacing fields; tokenless writes may only create new rows. At minimum merge fields instead of replacing so junk keys can't destroy existing answers.
